newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may stop vodka imports from Jan 1 - govt.
newsitem.headline: Russia may stop vodka imports from Jan 1 - govt.

text.p: Russia may stop imports of vodka and pure alcohol from January 1, 1997 as promised import licences and quotas have not yet been distributed, a Customs Committee official said on Friday.

"From January 1 customs officers will not let vodka and pure alcohol into Russia without quotas and licences," Yelena Tsvetkova, deputy head of the committee's indirect taxation department told a news conference.
The government earlier this year introduced 1997 import quotas for 100 million litres of strong liquors and 10 million litres of ethanol.
She said the government had set up a commission to distribute quotas to importers at the end of October, but it had not yet begun work.

The International Monetary Fund strongly objects to any quotas on alcohol imports and their planned introduction was one of the reasons why the IMF delayed payment in October of a tranche of its $10-billion loan to Russia.
Mikhail Vanin, head of the customs violations department, said the amount of alcohol smuggled into Russia had grown.
He said customs only manage to stop between 30 to 40 percent of smuggled drink.
Russian imports of alcoholic drinks, worth $736 million, were 34 percent lower in the first nine months of this year than in the same period of 1995.
Vodka imports, which made up 17 percent of the total, fell by 52 percent to 38.74 million litres.
